request.name: stream_virtual_output_with_properties

description.summary: create a virtual display with explicit panel properties

request.description:
The name is a persistent, nonempty identifier for the receiving device, independent of its address and transport. The description is its user-visible name. Width and height are panel pixels, independent of scale. Refresh is in millihertz. Physical width and height are millimetres; both are zero when unknown.
Headset is zero for an ordinary monitor or one for a left-first split-eye display. A headset has an even panel width. Each eye uses half the panel width and the full panel height, with no intermediate full-width eye image. The stream contains the two eye viewports side by side at exactly the panel size. Scale is the UI scale of each viewport, not a multiplier of panel pixels.
A headset request explicitly selects the virtual side-by-side mode on first use. This is not automatic stereo mode selection merely because an output advertises stereo capability. Compatible saved placement and UI scale may be restored on subsequent use. An explicit later output-configuration request from the user may change the mode; the creation request does not restrict it. Identity, initial mode, refresh and viewports must be established before the output is announced. Lens distortion is the receiver's responsibility and is not applied to this stream.
Invalid or unsupported properties fail the stream and create no output. The compositor must not silently substitute a mono view, a different pixel size or a different refresh. Width, height, refresh and scale must be positive; headset must be zero or one. A client requiring these properties must not fall back to an older request when version 7 is unavailable. Closing the stream removes the output, as for the other virtual-output requests.
